question: Explain the methods of measuring national income.

points.label: Product (value added) method
points.description: National income is measured as the sum of gross value added by all producing units in the economy, i.e. value of output less intermediate consumption, across primary, secondary and tertiary sectors.

points.label: Avoiding double counting
points.description: Only final goods or value added are counted, not intermediate goods, to avoid counting the same output more than once.
points.basis: National income: problem of double counting

points.label: Income method
points.description: National income is the sum of factor incomes earned: compensation of employees, rent, interest, profit and mixed income of the self-employed.

points.label: Expenditure method
points.description: National income is measured from final expenditure: private final consumption, government final consumption, gross capital formation and net exports.

points.label: Adjustments and equality
points.description: To get national income (NNP at factor cost) from domestic product, depreciation and net indirect taxes are deducted and net factor income from abroad is added; in principle all three methods give the same figure.
points.basis: National income: aggregates and equality of the three methods
